Md Nazrul Islam with Syed Al-Ashafur Ali, Advocates—For the Plaintiffs-Petitioners. 
Harendra Nath Nandy with Md Sarafatullah, Advocates—For Opposite Party No. 1.
parties:
ASM Ziaul Hoque & ors ------ Plaintiffs-Petitioners
vs
Lutfar Rahman Molla ------ Defendant-Opposite Party
full_judgment:
These three Rules were issued in Civil Revision Nos. 2525 of 2005, 2526 of 2005 and 2527 of 2005 arising out of Title Appeal No. 145 of 1996 against the Title Suit No. 60 of 1994 (original Title Suit No. 180 of 1990), Civil Revision No. 2526 of 2005 arising out of Title Appeal No. 144 of 1996 against the Title Suit No. 16 of 1995 (original Title Suit No. 137 of 1994) and Civil Revision No. 2527 of 2005 arising out of Title Appeal No. 143 of 1996 against the Title Suit No. 72 of 1994 (original Title Suit No. 194 of 1990) calling upon the opposite party No. 1 to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 15-2-2005 and 22-2-2005 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Jhenidah, in Title Appeal Nos. 143 of 1996, 144 of 1996 and 145 of 1996 allowing the appeal and reversing the judgment and decree dated 30-6-1996 and 7796 respectively passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Additional Court, Jhenidah, in Title Suit Nos. 60 of 1994, 16 of 1995 and 72 of 1994 decreeing the suit should not be set aside.

2. Since the three appeals were heard and disposed of by one judgment so the three Rules were also disposed of by this single judgment.

3. The short fact of the case is that the plaintiffs-petitioners brought the Title Suit No. 180 of 1990 in the Court of learned Senior Assistant Judge, Additional Court, Jhenidah for a declaration that the ex parte decree passed in Title Suit No. 283 of 1988 on 3-6-1990 in favour of the respondent-opposite party in respect of 14 decimals of land under suit Plot No. 1057 of SA Khatian No. 90 of Mouza Teordah No. 254 was collusive, inoperative, illegal, void and not binding upon the plaintiff-petitioners who claimed themselves to be necessary parties was not in pleading in Title Suit No. 283 of 1988. Title Suit No. 283 of 1988 was brought by defendant-opposite party for declaration of his title in 14 decimals of said land. The said suit was transferred to the Court of learned Senior Assistant Judge, Additional Court, Jhenidah for trial and the Title Suit No. 180 of 1990 was renumbered as 60 of 1994.

4. The plaintiff-petitioners case, in brief, is that 25 decimals of land under SA Khatian No. 90, Mouza Teordah No. 254 was taken on lease by one Mubarak Mridha from CS recorded tenant Ratikanta and others. While he was possessing thereof he sold the same to Abdur Rashid Miah by a registered kabala dated 2-3-1965. While Abdur Rashid was in possession thereof by mutating his name and by payment of rent thereof he sold the same to the plaintiff petitioner Nos. 13 by three separate kabalas dated 12-11-86. The plaintiff-petitioner No. 4, the father of plaintiff-petitioner, possessed the suit land on their behalf along with other lands of the suit plot by paying rent and, by mutating their name and amalgamating the same with his other adjoining nonsuited lands under his own Plot Nos. 1058 and 1059 by establishing a paddy crushing mill and Chatal thereon. On 8-7-91 respondent-opposite party secretly managed to obtain the ex parte decree in Title Suit No. 283 of 1988 and thereafter threatened to dispossess the plaintiff-petitioners from the 14 decimals of said land by virtue of the said ex parte decree dated 3690. So the plaintiff-petitioners brought the Title Suit No. 180 of 1990 and thereafter the said suit was renumbered as Title Suit No. 60 of 1994 which was filed for declaration that the ex parte decree passed in Title Suit No. 283 of 1988 is not binding on them. The suit was dismissed by his judgment and decree dated 21-11-1991. The plaintiff-petitioners filed the Title Appeal No. 216 of 1991 against the dismissal order. The appeal was heard by the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Jhenidah who was pleased to allow the appeal and set aside the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court and by the said judgment the Title Suit No. 60 of 1994 was sent on remand to the Trial Court for fresh trial analogously with Title Suit No. 72 of 1994 (a suit brought by respondent-petitioner Lutfur Rahman for declaration of his title in 14 decimals of land and for partition by metes and bounds) by taking into consideration the evidence, documents already filed by either party and by giving an opportunity to the parties to adduce further oral evidence, if necessary. Accordingly, the Title Suit No. 60 of 1994 was analogously tried with Title Suit No. 72 of 1994 brought by the plaintiff-petitioners for their declaration of title in 14 decimals of land, all these three suits between the same parties over the same suit land.

5. The case of the defendant (respondent-opposite party) Lutfur Rahman is that the suit land along with other lands originally belonged to TC Tude under whom Rati Kanta and Makhan Sundari Dasya were the tenants. They defaulted in payment of rent, TC Tudi obtained a rent decree against them. Subsequently, he sold 14 decimals of said land to Didar Baksh and Chan Khan, Ratikanta and Makhan Sundari again defaulted in payment of rent and again the land was put to auction for sale on obtaining rent decree. Didar Baksh and Monaim purchased the same in auction and went into possession thereof. Thereafter, they sold 14 decimals of land to Abdul Gani on 20-6-60. While in possession thereof Abdul Gani sold the same to respondent-opposite party Lutfar Rahman who went into possession of the land and constructed building thereon. Plaintiff-petitioners threatened to dispossess Lutfar Rahman from the said building on 6th Sravan, 1397 BS so he brought the Title Suit No. 72 of 1994 and prayed for injunction, but show cause notices were served upon the plaintiff-petitioners but they constructed building on the said land in spite of serving of such notice. Plaintiff-petitioners were never in possession of the said 14 decimals of land before hand. The defendant-opposite party in their additional written statement also stated that the record of right in respect of the said land in the name of Mobarak Mridha was wrongly recorded. He also denied the allegation that Abdur Rashid was in possession of the said land. But the plaintiff-petitioners are in possession of the said land and by constructing godown and Chatal thereon. So, according to him, plaintiff-petitioner's false Title Suit No. 60 of 1994 and Title Suit No. 16 of 1995 are liable to be dismissed and the case brought by him as plaintiff being 'Title Suit No. 72 of 1994 needs to be decreed.

6. During the trial the Title Suit No. 60 of 1994 was dismissed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Jhenidah by his judgment and order dated 21-11-91.

7. Being aggrieved by the judgment and order of dismissal the plaintiff-petitioners filed an appeal being No. 45 of 1996 before the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Jhenidah, who after hearing the appeal was pleased to allow the appeal and set aside the judgment and order passed by the trial Court and sent the case on remand for fresh trial analogously with other two suits directing the trial Court to take further evidence and to hear the parties, if necessary.

8. The learned Senior Assistant Judge, Additional Court, Jhenidah tried the Title Suit No. 60 of 1994, Title Suit No. 72 of 1994 and 16 of 1995 analogously and by taking into consideration all the documents already filed and examining the evidence on record decreed the Title Suit No. 60 of 1994 and Title Suit No. 16 of 1995 brought by the plaintiff-petitioners and dismissed the Title Suit No. 72 of 1994. He also declared title of the plaintiff-petitioners to the said land and further declared that the ex parte decree passed in Title Suit No. 283 of 1988 is inoperative and not binding upon the plaintiff-petitioners by his judgment dated 30-6-96, in other words, the plaintiff-petitioners obtained the judgment and decree of both the cases in his favour and the case of the defendant-opposite parties were dismissed.

9. Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree the defendant-opposite party preferred the Title Appeal Nos. 143 of 1996, 144 of 1996 and 145 of 1996 against the judgment and decree of the learned Senior Assistant Judge. Additional Court, Jhenidah dated 30-6-96 in respect of Title Suit No.72 of 1994, Title Suit No. 16 of 1995 and Title Suit No. 60 of 1994 respectively. This revisional application is related to Title Appeal No; 145 of 1996 arising out of Title Suit No. 60 of 1994 which is in respect of plaintiff-petitioner's prayer for declaration that the ex parte decree obtained by the defendant-opposite party in Title Suit No. 283 of 1988 is not binding upon the plaintiff-petitioners. Thereafter, the lower Appellate Court heard all the three appeals analogously being Title Appeal Nos. 143 of 1996, arising out of Title Suit No. 72 of 1994, Title Appeal No. 144 of 1996 arising out of Title Suit No. 16 of 1995, Title Appeal No. 145 of 1996 arising out of Title Suit No. 60 of 1994. The learned lower appellate Court allowed all the appeals and set aside the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court and in Title Appeal No. 143 of 1996 on the prayer of the appellants lawyer before the Appellate Court who submitted that as a matter of fact the lawyer who conducted the Title Suit No. 72 of 1994 before the trial Court could not produce some important documents and the plaint also needs to be amended, therefore, if the appeal is sent on remand to the trial Court for proper adjudication of the eases justice would be met. On the prayer of the lawyer of the appellants of Title Appeal No. 143 of 1996 the lower appellate Court sent all the appeals on remand to the trial Court for fresh trial directing the trial Court by giving an opportunity to both the parties to adduce evidence and produce documents and amend the plaint, if necessary.

10. Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree dated 15-2-2005 and 22-2-2005 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Jhenidah, in Title Appeal Nos. 143 of 1996, 144 of 1996 and 145 of 1996 allowing the appeal and reversing the judgment and decree dated 30-6-96 and 7-7-96 respectively passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Additional Court Jhenidah, in Title Suit Nos. 60 of 1994, 16 of 1995 and 72 of 1994 the respondent-petitioner preferred the instant revisional application before the High Court Division under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the present Rule.

11. Mr Muhammad Nazrul Islam with Mr Syed Al-Asafur Ali, appearing on behalf of the respondent-petitioners, submits that the learned lower appellate Court is absolutely wrong and erroneous in sending the case back on remand unnecessarily for fresh trial which will take a long time to dispose of the suit causing hardship to parties. Next, he submits that the appellate Court committed an error of law by passing further order of allowing fresh evidence when fresh evidence has already been adduced by the plaintiff-petitioners and also examined more witnesses by the plaintiff-petitioners and the defendants also. He further submits that the lower appellate Court committed an error of law by giving an opportunity to the defendant-opposite party to fill up the lacuna by taking fresh evidence who miserably failed to prove his case even at the time of fresh trial earlier when the case was remanded for retrial in Title Appeal No. 216 of 1991. The learned Counsel finally, submits that the lower appellate Court only to shirk his responsibility sent the case on remand for fresh trial to the trial Court where there is a Provision under section 117 of the Code of Civil Procedure that the appellate Court is absolutely empowered to examine and take evidence, if necessary, for proper adjudication instead of sending the case back to the trial Court for causing unnecessary delay.

12. On the other hand, the learned Counsel Mr Harendra Nath Nandy with Mr Md Sarafatullah, appearing on behalf of the appellant-opposite party, submits that if the suits are sent on remand to the lower appellate Court without sending these to trial Court for fresh trial this will be more expedient. He conceded to the submission of the learned lawyer of the petitioner that a direction may kindly be given to the lower appellate Court to dispose of the appeals in accordance with law, if necessary, by taking the evidence or examining the witnesses by the appellate Court itself, without sending the suits to the trial Court.

<u>13. On a meticulous examination of the evidence on record, documents and other connected papers and after hearing the submission of both the parties it appears to me that if the case is sent to lower appellate Court for expeditious hearing of the appeals instead of sending the cases to the trial Court for fresh trial and for proper adjudication justice would be met. In this connection, I like to refer the decision in the case of AR Abul Bashar Chowdhury vs Upazila Nirbahi Officer reported in 1992 BLD 662 ref 1986 BLD (AD) 135 wherein it has been held:</u>

<u>"Appellate Court being the final Court of facts the entire evidence, both oral and documentary, are sufficiently before him and there is no necessity for sending the case for fresh trial on flimsy ground".</u>

14. In view of the discussion made above and the facts and circumstances of the case and also the legal position, the judgment and decree dated 15-2-2005 and 22-2-2005 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Jhenidah, in Title Appeal No. 145 of 1996 heard analogously with Title Appeal Nos. 143 of 1996 and 144 of 1996 allowing the appeal and reversing the judgment and decree dated 30696 and 7796 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Additional Court, Jhenidah, in Title Suit Nos. 60 of 1994 heard analogously with Title Suit No. 16 of 1995 and 72 of 1994 decreeing the suit and the order of remand for sending the suits to the trial. Court for fresh trial is hereby set aside and the lower appellate Court is directed to rehear the appeals as expeditiously as possible preferably within 3(three) months and dispose of the appeals in accordance with law, if necessary, by examining witnesses and taking additional evidence, without sending the suits to the trial Court for fresh trial.

15. In the result, all the three Rules are disposed of in the light of the above observations.

16. The order of stay granted earlier by this Court at the time of issuance of the Rule is hereby vacated.

Lower Court's records be sent down at once with a copy of the judgment.

End.
